title: Recording 'Sugar' in Germany compared with Victor and the Canadian studio
summary: The German studio's microphones and technique impressed him more than Victor's or the small Canadian studios; hearing the playback he thought it perhaps the best record he had made.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: : Okay, we can do that, right. But meanwhile, this was a two-day recording session in Germany.
Yeah, I -- yes.
: How did it go? Was it easy?
Oh, it was beautiful.
: Hard?
No, it was very -- it was very -- of all the years that I spent at Victor, Victor's recording, you know --
: With Fats.

Yeah, and there were two or three guys, I mean Victor at that time, was supposed to be the best. I mean -- I heard about Decca, and all of those places, and they were -- they weren't supposed to even hold a candle to Victor.
: You recorded at Decca, too, didn't you?
Well, with Sammy Price --
Sammy, right.
-- and a couple of other people. You know. We did -- you didn't mention those.
(Laughter.)
I didn't.
But the Victors were different.

Oh, Victor, yeah. But man, when we got to Germany there, and naturally I had never been there, and I'd never seen a place like that, and they have so many mikes! Everywhere I looked there was a mike. Each trumpet, each man had his own mike, and we didn't have them -- the way they went about it, and as long as we stayed there, I stayed there knowing that these guys was supposed to be the best they had on the job, an Oscar, something like that, they had an Oscar for the best for the year, you know?
And --
That's a great studio there. I've heard of it.
Yeah, and they was great. I mean they got it for being the best -- greatest of all recording artists, and -- I mean the technique and stuff that they had there, and how great it was.
When you recorded in Canada, you made two records in Canada, didn't you? Or one?
Yes.
Two?
Uh-huh.
Was that in a studio, or was that in a club?
In a studio.
In a studio? But the studio wasn't as big and didn't have as many microphones.
No, there wasn't as much know-how, and whatnot, and it wasn't too good.
It was a smaller operation.

It was -- I appreciated, because I was glad to be -- at least you're moving, you know, to my mind, as long as you're doing something, and you might not be a hit, but well, you're in there trying, you know what I mean.

But these people here in Germany, oh man! They were such nice guys to work with, and they knew what they -- you could see they knew what they were doing, and when the playback came, that's what knocked me off my feet. I mean I heard so much. I said boy! Is that us? Because I said for six guys, sounding like this? Impossible.
Do you think this is the best record you ever made?
(Sighs.) By golly, I might. (Laughs.) I went -- and I'm tempted to say yes. Because of their know-
how, and they way -- what they did, you know, not that I did.
In addition to what you did.
Yeah. Uh-huh.
But you feel these were better than the records you made with Fats?
Well that's what I'm trying to say, because I mean there's the knowhow of the techniques, and the mechanical doings, and whatnot, and all that stuff. I have -- I liked it. I appreciated it.
